# xtx

> Exact and fast model matrices for R, and model fitting on them (xtx.fit).

## Pages

- [Architecture](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/architecture.html): This page describes how xtx is built, for readers who want to know where a result comes from or where to look in the source. File names refer to the repository.
- [Benchmarks](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/benchmarks.html): How much time does it save to skip the dense model matrix? This page times six common operations twice: once with base R, which builds the full matrix first, and once with xtx, which works from the design matrix instead. The data have 200,000 rows, the model matrix has 119…
- [Fixed effects](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/fit/fixed_effects.html): Fixed effects go after a | in the formula, as in fixest. The same model, fitted with both packages on a dataset that comes with fixest:
- [glm_xtx()](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/fit/glm_xtx.html): glm_xtx() fits a generalized linear model like glm(), without the dense model matrix. The same model with both, on a dataset that comes with R:
- [Leverage](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/fit/leverage.html): The hat values of a linear model are the diagonal of X (X'X)^-1 X', and (X'X)^-1 is vcov(fit) / sigma(fit)^2.
- [lm_xtx()](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/fit/lm_xtx.html): lm_xtx() fits a linear model like lm(), without the dense model matrix. The same model with both, on a dataset that comes with R:
- [Standard errors](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/fit/standard_errors.html): lm_xtx() and glm_xtx() take vcov = "iid" (the default) or vcov = ~cl, for standard errors clustered by a variable. The last section computes heteroskedasticity-consistent and clustered covariance matrices for data that stay in a database.
- [Introduction](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/): The xtx package builds model matrices that are identical, bit for bit, to those returned by stats::model.matrix(), and computes products, sums and quadratic forms of them without forming the dense matrix. It is an extremely fast way to compute design matrices and compute standard…
- [Operations](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/operations.html): This page lists what you can do with a design matrix, with columns and with groupings. The Algebra recipes check each result against base R, and Benchmarks times the operations.
- [Out-of-core data](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/out-of-core.html): When the data do not fit in memory, they can stay in Parquet files or in a DuckDB table. Here d is a data frame and "d.parquet" a file with the same rows. The code does not change: only the data argument does. The rows are never read into R: products with the design run in the…
- [Algebra](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/recipes/algebra.html): These examples go with the tables on the Operations page. Each one checks a small result against base R, with identical() when the result is exact and all.equal() when sums run in a different order. The benchmarks run on the benchmark setup, in a fresh R process each.
- [Estimators](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/recipes/package-developers.html): These recipes build estimators from the columns and groupings. Each one is written once and runs on a data frame and on a database table. The remote examples need the DBI and duckdb packages.
- [Prediction](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/recipes/prediction.html): These recipes compute predictions from a fitted model and their standard errors. Both build the design for the new data from the model's own encoding, so they rely on reusing a design on new data. Each one checks a small example against base R, then times both on 200,000 rows and…
- [glm_xtx](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference-fit/glm_xtx.html): glm_xtx() fits a generalized linear model by iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS), like stats::glm(), without forming the dense model matrix. It takes a formula and a data frame, a xtx::design_matrix() and a response y (like stats::glm.fit()), or remote data (see Remote…
- [lm_xtx](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference-fit/lm_xtx.html): lm_xtx() fits a linear model by least squares, like stats::lm(), without forming the dense model matrix. Given a xtx::design_matrix() and a response y instead of a formula and data, it fits that design, like stats::lm.fit().
- [remote_fits](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference-fit/remote_fits.html): The fit is the same algorithm as in memory, on remote primitives: with few design patterns it is compressed (see Compression in xtx::design_remote); otherwise it solves the normal equations of the remote design (X'WX in the database, suspect columns judged from products with the…
- [Summary.xtx_column](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/column_arithmetic.html): Base R functions work on the columns of a design (see design_column): in memory a column is a numeric vector, and remotely a design_column has methods for the same functions, which compute in the database and return the same values as base R on the vector. Together with…
- [%*%.xtx_matrix](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/design_algebra.html): Products with a design_matrix are computed directly from the factor codes and numeric variables, with the usual base R operators:
- [Ops.xtx_matrix](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/design_arithmetic.html): Scaling rows and adding or subtracting design matrices gives another design_matrix, still without forming the dense matrix. Row i of the result is s1[i] * x1_i + s2[i] * x2_i, where x1_i and x2_i are rows of at most two designs with the same rows and columns.
- [[.xtx_column](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/design_column.html): A column holds one value per row of a design. In memory it is a plain numeric vector. For a remote design (see design_remote), it is a design_column: a lazy SQL expression over the rows of the design, which nothing evaluates until its values are asked for. Products with a remote…
- [design_frame](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/design_frame.html): design_frame() takes the arguments of stats::model.frame() and returns the same model frame, faster on large data. design_matrix() uses it to build its model frames. When data is remote data (a DuckDB connection, or Parquet paths), it returns the remote frame of the model…
- [design_groups](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/design_groups.html): A grouping gives each row of a design the number of its group, from the values of one or more key variables: integer codes 1..G, one per level of the key. Grouped sums, crosstabs, lookups of a value per group and nesting tests then work from the codes, in memory and on a remote…
- [design_matrix](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/design_matrix.html): design_matrix() takes the same arguments as stats::model.matrix() and returns a design_matrix object: the prepared variables plus everything needed to build the matrix (column names, contrasts, term layout). The dense matrix is built by as.matrix(), and algebra such as design %*%…
- [design_parts](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/design_parts.html): design_parts() extracts from a fitted model the pieces that design_matrix(model, newdata = ) needs to build the model matrix of new data: the terms, the levels of the factors and the contrasts. Each method reads the pieces that the model's own predict() method uses.
- [design_patterns](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/design_patterns.html): design_patterns() groups the rows of a design that have the same row of the model matrix (and, with keys, the same values of the key columns) into patterns, and summarizes a response z within each pattern: the sum of the weights, the weighted mean, and the weighted sum of squares…
- [design_qr](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/design_qr.html): qr(x) decomposes a design_matrix as X P = Q R without forming the dense matrix X or the n by p matrix Q. It returns an object of class "xtx_qr", which the usual base R functions accept: qr.coef(), qr.fitted(), qr.resid(), qr.qty(), qr.qy(), qr.Q(), qr.R() and solve(). This gives…
- [design_relation](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/design_relation.html): design_relation() gives what a query needs to read columns over the rows of a remote design: the connection, the source to select from, the filter of the rows and the SQL expression of each column. It is for computations that stay in the database (tables of sums within the levels…
- [coerce,xtx_remote,CsparseMatrix-method](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/design_remote.html): With a DBI connection to DuckDB, or the path of Parquet files, as data, design_matrix() returns a remote design: the rows stay in the database, and products with the design run there, so that data larger than memory can be used.
- [coerce,xtx_matrix,CsparseMatrix-method](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/sparse.html): as(x, "CsparseMatrix") (or as(x, "dgCMatrix")) builds a sparse column-compressed matrix (a Matrix::dgCMatrix) from a design matrix, without forming the dense matrix. The non-zero values are those of as.matrix(), bit for bit; exact zeros are dropped and NA and NaN are kept. The…
- [[.xtx_matrix](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/xtx/reference/sub-.xtx_matrix.html): x[i, ] keeps the rows i of a design matrix, without forming the dense matrix: the factor codes and numeric variables of the selected rows are copied, and every product and summary works on the result as on any other design. For a design built by applying a plan to newdata…
